display_title: kriegmate: Adversarial Monte Carlo COA Analysis
one_liner: A terrain-aware stochastic combat simulation (company team to brigade) wrapped in a full simulation-analysis toolkit: paired COA comparison with CRN, Kim-Nelson selection, GP and Sobol sensitivity, and rung-by-rung history-matching calibration. The parameters are notional: the model is verified but not validated.
problem: Comparing courses of action with a stochastic combat model is only useful if the comparison is statistically honest (paired, interval-bounded, selection-bias-aware), the discretization is checked, and the parameters have a defined path from notional to calibrated.
approach: An entity engine runs on OSM or DEM or synthetic ground: detection hazard, multinomial-logit target choice, circular-normal hit probability, suppression, and Beta breakpoints. It uses named random substreams so COAs share random numbers. Around it sit Wilson/delta/sup-t intervals, Kaplan-Meier and Aalen-Johansen for censored outcomes, Kim-Nelson ranking-and-selection, a Latin hypercube design with a stochastic-kriging GP and Saltelli/Jansen Sobol indices, and history matching (implausibility, NROY waves) with a held-out terrain coverage check. An aggregate brigade engine is derived as a mean-field limit of the entity kill chain and bias-corrected against it.
decision_relevance: Supports COA analysis (which Blue scheme of maneuver is best, with what confidence) and shows the V&V and calibration process that Army analytic organizations apply to combat models. The outputs are methodological, not operational, because every parameter is notional.

headline_results.claim: Paired comparison with common random numbers: support-by-fire 0.678 [0.658, 0.699] vs maneuver 0.649 [0.628, 0.670], n=2000 each; paired difference +0.029 [+0.009, +0.050]; CRN halved the variance

Grid cell size is not converged: the 25 m vs 12.5 m gap is 0.169 at a 7.5 s tick (non-overlapping intervals), larger than the tactical effect the model measures, so absolute probabilities are partly a grid artifact
43 of 47 test suites pass in 10 min 55 s, backing the verified-claims table
Sobol sensitivity: probability of kill at tank range dominates (total-order 0.61-0.79), metamodel LOO R2 0.75-0.86

limitations: Parameters are notional; nothing is fitted to or checked against real data
Absolute win probabilities are partly a grid artifact; only fixed-cell paired comparisons are defensible
Brigade table runs at n=20 replications; raising it costs about an hour of CPU
blockers_before_featuring: OWNER DECISION: notional force-quality and C2 scores for Russia, China and Iran (sim/nations.py, sim/c2.py) — confirm no prepublication/PAO review is required (DoDI 5230.29)
Cell size is not converged; no absolute probability from this model should appear as a result until the sweep extends to 6.25 m
